data.text:
Good, I can see the structure. The key insight is that `customer_id` in orders is per order (one per order), while `customer_unique_id` identifies the same person across multiple orders. So I need to join on `customer_id` and then group by `customer_unique_id`.

Let me run the SQL query:

args.purpose: Count customers who placed more than one order, counting all orders regardless of status
args.sql:
SELECT 
    c.customer_unique_id,
    COUNT(o.order_id) as order_count
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
HAVING COUNT(o.order_id) > 1
